explanation: The E138G substitution eliminates a negatively charged, bulky glutamate residue in the palm domain, removing a critical electrostatic interaction or conformational stabilizing element that maintains the NNRTI-binding pocket geometry ~43 Å away. Glycine's flexibility and loss of the extended side chain (78.3 Ų decrease) permits subtle backbone repositioning in the palm that propagates distortion of the allosteric binding pocket, compromising van der Waals contacts and hydrogen bond networks required for efavirenz recognition without directly contacting the ligand. This indirect mechanism—wherein a remote, negatively-charged residue acts as a structural scaffold—explains the modest but measurable resistance (ΔΔG = +0.005 kcal/mol) arising from loss of electrostatic and steric constraints rather than direct steric clash.
